guide.a.what_are_email_notifications:
When set up, this site can send two emails after each booking:

  • a confirmation email to the attendee, with their ticket details and link, if they gave an email address;
  • a notification email to your business email address, if you have set one, so you know someone booked.

Emails are sent in the background, so they never slow down a booking.
guide.q.supported_email_providers: Which email companies work with this site?
guide.a.supported_email_providers:
This site cannot send emails on its own — a normal email account blocks you after a few hundred, because it looks like spam. So emails go through a company built for sending lots of them.

Five companies are supported:

  • Resend
  • Postmark
  • SendGrid
  • Mailgun (US)
  • Mailgun (EU)

They all work the same way here. Pick one you already have an account with, or one whose free amount covers how many emails you send.
guide.q.setup_email: How do I set up email?
guide.q.test_email_working: How do I test that email is working?
guide.a.test_email_working:
After saving your email settings, a Send Test Email button appears. Click it to send a test email to your business email address.

If the test fails, you see the error message from your email company. That message usually names the fix — most often a wrong key, or a "from" address the company does not know about yet.
guide.q.email_not_configured: What if email is not set up?
guide.a.email_not_configured: Email is completely optional. With no email company chosen, this site simply sends no emails. Bookings, payments, and everything else work as normal.
guide.q.confirmation_email_content: What does the confirmation email contain?
guide.a.confirmation_email_content:
The attendee receives the listing name or names, the quantity, the price paid, and a link to their ticket page.

Each email also carries a picture of the ticket with its QR code — the square barcode scanned at the door. Listings set to No check-in leave the QR code out, because nobody will be scanned. A multi-listing booking gets one email listing everything, with one ticket picture per listing.

Your business email is the reply-to address, so attendees can reply straight to you.
guide.q.admin_notification_email_content: What does the notification email contain?
guide.a.admin_notification_email_content: You receive the attendee's name, email, phone, address, and any special instructions, along with the listing name or names, the quantity, and the price. The attendee's email is the reply-to address, so you can reply straight to them.
guide.q.customise_emails: Can I change the words in the emails?
guide.a.customise_emails:
Yes. In Advanced Settings, scroll to the email template sections. You can change both the confirmation email (sent to the attendee) and the notification email (sent to you). Each has three parts: the subject line, the HTML body, and the plain text body.

Templates are written in Liquid, a way of putting booking details into text. Each form lists the placeholders it accepts under Available variables. Clear any field to go back to the built-in wording.
guide.q.template_variables: What placeholders can I use in templates?
guide.q.template_error: What happens if my template has an error?
guide.a.template_error: If a custom template fails, this site falls back to the built-in wording automatically. The email still goes out — your attendees still get their confirmation.
guide.q.how_do_i_email_a_group_of: How do I email a group of attendees?
guide.a.how_do_i_email_a_group_of:
Open Emails in the top navigation (owners only), or click Email Attendees on a listing page to message that listing's attendees.

Choose who receives it, write your message, tick marketing if it promotes something, then click Preview. The preview shows the finished email, the exact number of people receiving it, and what kind of message it is — before you send.
guide.a.who_can_i_send_to:
From a listing page, the recipients are that listing's attendees. From the Emails page you pick an audience:

  • Active listing attendees — everyone booked on a listing that is running now (the default).
  • Upcoming listing attendees — everyone booked on a listing that has not happened yet.
  • All attendees — everyone who has ever booked.

In every case, only attendees who gave an email address are included, and repeated addresses count once.
guide.a.how_does_unsubscribing_work:
Every marketing email ends with an unsubscribe link. It opens a page where the reader can stop receiving marketing emails (or start again) with one click — no password needed. Nothing happens until they press the button on that page.

The link works through a secret code made from their address, so the page never shows the address itself.

Unsubscribing only affects marketing emails. Messages about a booking they made still reach everyone.
guide.q.what_is_the_bcc_email_app_option: What is the BCC email-app option?
guide.a.what_is_the_bcc_email_app_option:
On the preview page there is always an option to open the email in your own email program, with the subject and message already filled in.

When it goes to several people, they all go in the BCC field, so nobody sees anyone else's address. A single person is addressed normally. It needs no set-up, so it works even when system sending is off.

Use it sparingly. Sending lots of mail this way, especially marketing, can get your own email account blocked. It is best for small, important messages.
guide.q.why_do_i_need_my_own_email: Why do I need my own email company to send?
guide.a.why_do_i_need_my_own_email:
Bulk email goes through your own email company, never a shared address. Sending marketing from a shared address could get every site on this platform labelled as spam.

If you have not added your own company (under Advanced Settings → Email), the Send button stays off — but the BCC email-app option above still works.
guide.q.what_s_the_difference_between_a_: What's the difference between a marketing and a service email?
guide.a.what_s_the_difference_between_a_:
A service email is information someone needs because they booked — a venue change, a reminder, cancellation details. A marketing email promotes something — a new listing, an offer, a newsletter.

When you tick marketing, every email gets an unsubscribe link at the bottom, and anyone who unsubscribed is skipped automatically. Service emails get no link and reach everyone.

Only tick marketing for real promotions. Calling a promotion a service email to dodge the unsubscribe rules can break anti-spam laws (such as GDPR/PECR or CAN-SPAM).
guide.q.can_i_see_how_often_i_ve: Can I see how often I've contacted someone?
guide.a.can_i_see_how_often_i_ve:
Yes. Each attendee's page shows an Email History — how many bulk emails they have received, when they were last contacted, and the last subject. Use it to avoid over-emailing people.

When you preview a bulk email, a line shows how often that audience has been contacted on average.

Counts cover bulk emails only, not the automatic confirmations sent after each booking.
